junction.name: Bruckner Boulevard & East 138 Street, New York City

claims.text: Bruckner Boulevard & East 138 Street had 126 injury crashes in police records since 2021-10-31: 19 pedestrians injured, 5 cyclists injured and 4 people killed.
At the U.S. DOT's values that harm costs about $8.6 million a year.
41% of crashes here happened in the rush hours, against 32% at the city's priority junctions.
35% of crashes here had only people in vehicles hurt, against 24% at the city's priority junctions.
6% of crashes here had “unsafe lane changing” recorded as a contributing factor, against 2% at the city's priority junctions.

Held up on later years: a vehicle was going straight ahead, heading north in 55% of crashes since 2024-05-01, against 19% at the city's priority junctions (found by the AI analyst and the greedy search and the exhaustive search).

Held up on later years: a vehicle was going straight ahead and it happened in the daytime in 62% of crashes since 2024-05-01, against 43% at the city's priority junctions (found by the greedy search and the exhaustive search).

The city's Leading Pedestrian Interval signals: worked (pedestrian injury crashes changed -17% (95% interval -22% to -11%) at 1,651 sites against sites treated later or the citywide trend, and a placebo date shows nothing).
The city's turn traffic calming: earlier trend (a simple before/after says -26%, but a placebo date before the work shows a drop too, so the decline cannot be credited to the program).
The city's enhanced crossings: not shown (at 96 sites the change in pedestrian injury crashes (-7%, 95% interval -50% to +69%) could be zero).
The city's speed humps: not shown (at 1,008 sites the change in injury crashes (+0%, 95% interval -9% to +9%) could be zero).

Backplates with Retroreflective Borders would avoid about 3.8 crashes a year (CMF 1410, the record FHWA's fact sheet cites; evidence: only if a site check confirms it), worth $1.3 million a year; check on site: an entry on yellow or red.

Yellow Change Intervals would avoid about 2.0 crashes a year (CMF 4219, the more conservative of the two middle records of 4; evidence: only if a site check confirms it), worth $673,000 a year; check on site: an entry on yellow or red; the current yellow plus all-red time is below the ITE recommended practice.
The New York State Department of Transportation (NYSDOT), Region 11 is responsible for Bruckner Expressway (I 278) (owner recorded in NYSDOT Roadway Inventory).
The NYC Department of Transportation (NYC DOT) is responsible for Bruckner Boulevard, East 138 Street (not listed in NYSDOT Roadway Inventory, so a city street).
Who can push for it: Council Member, District 8, New York City Council; Bronx Community Board 1.
A request letter to the New York State Department of Transportation (NYSDOT), Region 11 and the NYC Department of Transportation (NYC DOT) is drafted and checked.

draft_request.letter:
To: the New York State Department of Transportation (NYSDOT), Region 11; the NYC Department of Transportation (NYC DOT)
Cc: Council Member, District 8, New York City Council; Bronx Community Board 1
Subject: Request for safety study at Bruckner Boulevard & East 138 Street

Dear colleagues at NYSDOT Region 11 and NYC DOT,

We write about the junction of Bruckner Boulevard & East 138 Street.

Over the 5 years from 31 October 2021, official records for this junction show 296 crashes, including 126 injury crashes. Nineteen pedestrians and 5 cyclists were injured and 4 people were killed. The latest recorded safety project here is a Leading Pedestrian Interval signal in 2016, and there is no recorded treatment in the 5-year period. By the NYC Department of Transportation (NYC DOT), this junction is recorded as a city priority location.

By the U.S. DOT's official values for the cost of crashes (2024 dollars), the harm in this period is valued at $8.6 million per year.

We ask each road owner to carry out a safety study at the junction for the roads it is responsible for — NYSDOT Region 11 for Bruckner Expressway (I 278) and NYC DOT for Bruckner Boulevard and East 138 Street — and to confirm what can be delivered on those roads.

Please review:

• Longer yellow signal times (federal name: Yellow Change Intervals) may avoid about 6.9 injury crashes per year, avoiding about $2,347,000 in harm per year. This requires a site check for an entry on yellow or red.

• Reflective backplates on the traffic signals (federal name: Backplates with Retroreflective Borders) may avoid about 3.8 injury crashes per year, avoiding about $1,294,000 in harm per year. This requires a site check for an entry on yellow or red.

Please consider implementation on each agency's roads where the site checks support it.

Yours sincerely,

[Your name]
[Your organisation or address]
